title: The elevator has a ninth floor 🛗

hook_text: At 2:40 in the morning my elevator showed a button for a ninth floor.

scenes.narration: At 2:40 in the morning my elevator showed a button for a ninth floor.
My building has eight. I have lived here for six years. The button was pale yellow, and warm.
I pressed it. Not because I wanted to. My hand had decided before I did.
The doors closed. The numbers climbed. Seven. Eight. Then the display went blank, and kept climbing.
The doors opened on a corridor exactly like mine. Same carpet. Same flickering light. Same door at the end.
The last door was open. Inside, my sweater hung on a chair. My mug was still steaming.
My bed was made, with a dent in it. A dent still warm from someone who had just stood up.
Behind me the lift spoke for the first time in six years. Welcome home. Floor eight was only where you slept.
The doors began to close. And in the last gap of light, I saw the person standing in the elevator. Wearing my sweater.
So tell me. Do you press the button, or take the stairs?
